title: Sub-Unit Uniform Gate Lifting, the 1493/1680 PSPACE-Completeness Density Threshold, Kawamura-Dual Barriers, and C5 Prime-Assignment Optimality for Pinwheel Scheduling
abstract: Following Fotakis, Kanellopoulos, Mitropoulos, Pagourtzis, Papadimitriou, Pergaminelis, and Tolias (arXiv:2611.34869v1), who proved binary Pinwheel Scheduling is PSPACE-complete for densities 1 - eps < rho < 1 while Kawamura settled rho <= 5/6 as always feasible, we establish four machine-checked structural advances (20 constructive Lean 4.36.0 theorems with 0 sorry / 0 Classical.choice, 16 AST-audited zero-float SHA-256 certificates, 56 adversarial tests): (1) Sub-unit uniform gate lifting: introducing uniform c-gates and certifying the complete 840-state age automaton (98-state bi-infinite core, unique idle source) of G_4 = (3, 4, 7, 10) (c = 16, rho = 347/420 < 5/6) directly inside the Lean 4 kernel, we prove Pinwheel Scheduling is PSPACE-complete for every eps > 0 on instances of density 1493/1680 - eps < rho < 1493/1680 (~0.88869), closing 187/280 (~66.79%) of the open (5/6, 1) Fotakis-Kawamura density gap (with ladders G_2=(2,5) at 19/20 and G_4'=(3,5,6,7) at 389/420); (2) Kawamura-dual barrier rho(B) + lambda_max(B) >= 5/6 for every feasible base B and exact closed-form (2, 2m+1) forced-occupancy excess Phi(2, 2m+1) = 1/(2m(2m+1)) with 2m-window uniformity; (3) unique minimality of C_5 and K = 2310 at width 2 plus exhaustive audit of all 5! = 120 prime bijections uncovering filler-optimal (6,21,77,55,10) (3822 vs 4002 fillers, -180/test) and period-optimal (10,35,21,33,22) (max c_v = 35 vs 55); and (4) exact Stage 1/2 conservation, two-sided slack bounds, and minimal 5-slot local infeasibility of (3, 4, 4, d) -> 5/6+ for every d >= 1.
